text: when students die during a school-sponsored team-building activity, responsibility typically falls on the organizing coaches/school staff, the school administration, and potentially the resort operators for failing to exercise proper diligence and safety protocols. the people responsible for the team building activity should answer these questions: - was there a formal and robust pre-activity risk assessment conducted to identify all potential risks that may cause harm to participating students? this is very basic and if this was not done, it is already a good starting point to build a case involving school negligence. - for the risks identified, what mitigation measures were to taken to eliminate or minimize the risk? - are there weather contigencies and equipment inspections conducted prior to the team-building? - are there comprehensive health screenings performed to determine if the students are fit for the activities scheduled? - are students allowed to opt out of specific physical activites without penalties if they feel unsafe? - were safety briefings done at the start of the team building activity? - what is the ratio of the supervising staff to students? - is a trained first aid responder present? this is typically needed if the team building includes physical activities. - in the team building conducted in previouis years, was there an anonymous formal feedback system where students can report feeling unsafe or harassed during the activities? - if the students are minors, were approval from the parents received? both student and parental sign-offs on behavior contracts and liability waivers are required before departure. deaths from school-sponsored team-building activity are mostly preventable. even if this was an accident and they have been doing this for years, there must be a thorough investigation on the degree of negligence involved. schools can be sued if a death occurs, provided it was a direct result of the school's negligence, breach of contract, or failure to maintain a reasonable standard of care. when a school accepts a student, it enters into an implied contract to provide a safe learning environment, extending to both on-campus actions and school-sponsored off-site activities like team building.
